usage: workit uninstall [--hosts=<h,…> [--preview | --yes]]

No flags: the interactive picker (hosts and the owned CLI install). --hosts takes claude-code, codex, cursor, opencode, pi; --preview prints the files, config keys and host commands it would remove and changes nothing; --yes removes them. Only the user runs --yes or the picker, in their own terminal; an agent may run --preview.

A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).

part.text:
I ran the preview (the only uninstall step an agent is permitted to run):

```console
$ workit uninstall --hosts=cursor --preview
cursor edit-json-remove ~/.cursor/settings.json
  remove workit enabled_plugins/plugin_dirs entries
  - enabled_plugins.workit
cursor edit-json-remove ~/.cursor/mcp.json
  remove the workit MCP server registration
  - mcpServers.workit
cursor remove-dir ~/.cursor/plugins/local/workit
  delete the local workit plugin directory
your Workit configuration ... is always kept
Preview: nothing changed.
```

Nothing was changed. `workit uninstall` deliberately refuses to let an agent apply the removal: `--yes` and the interactive picker must be run by you, in your own terminal. I can't self-approve that, so the final step is yours:

```bash
workit uninstall --hosts=cursor --yes
```

Scope is Cursor only, so Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi are untouched; Workit's config is kept either way.
